$description: Design tokens for every DCC app, in the W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) shape: each token has a $value and a $type. Dark is the designed theme: a colour's $value is its dark value, and $extensions.dcc.light is the light value derived from it (spec §6.2). Palette direction B, Dungeon brass, chosen 2026-09-27. Hex values are ours; a colour's MEANING is cited where the book prints it.

contrast.$description: Every pair a screen may put together, and the WCAG 2.1 minimum it must meet in both themes. 4.5 is AA for text; 3 is AA for large text, control boundaries, focus indicators, and graphics a user needs (1.4.11). The repo's tests fail if any pair falls short.

pairs.why: The accent is also used as text: a formula, a link
The primary action's label
The corner marks on a band or window are graphics
The System's voice is text: a notification's kicker, a readout's name line
A window's frame
Inputs and Hotlist slots are identified by their frame
A field's frame around its own fill
A filled slot must read as filled; the count and text value are also always shown (spec §6.3)
A filled slot against an emptied one
The Mana Bar empties to the same track colour
A Spell's Mana cost on its Hotlist tile is text
A skill row's check-type edge and symbol; the type is also in words on the row (law 16)
A die's numeral is text on the die, which keeps its colour in both themes
Bone, and Marble, whose veins are kept clear of the numeral so it sits on the Bone body
The Journal look: the shared colours again on its own grounds
The inked frame of a box or a row
A slot left, against the page and a spent one
A spent movement step keeps its frame
MENU and the folder on the binding
A name stamped on a cover on the shelf
A cover's tooled frame and a blank cover's photo mounts, graphics in the stitching's line
The words on a label plate on the sheet: Cast, a to-hit, a damage roll, Check, Save
A used group's plates, and a roll's label on its plate
The rule inside a plate, its edge as a control
A to-hit's and New turn's doubled rule, a graphic; never words on the plate
Short Rest and Long Rest on their seals
A seal is a button, known by its wax
A spell slot left, and a spent one's outline; the count is also in words (spec §6.3)
A slot left beside a spent one
A class resource's use left, and a spent one's outline; the count is also in words

dcc.note: Light is aged, yellowed parchment (user, 2026-10-19, direction B, Oxblood and ink).

surface.$description: A panel or band on the canvas: the HUD wrapper, a card

surface-raised.$description: A row, slot, or field inside a surface

border.$description: Decorative hairline between regions. Never the only thing that identifies a control

dcc.note: Ink brown in light and a muted bronze in dark (direction B, 2026-10-19), in place of the classic brass #8a6d45.

border-control.$description: The frame that identifies a control or a slot, like ink ruling on an old page. Meets 3:1

dcc.note: The control frame's ink brown in light and a lighter bronze in dark (direction B, 2026-10-19), in place of the classic brass. Marks only, never a fill.

hud.$description: The HUD's frame: the short corner marks on the bands and windows

dcc.note: The book sets its chapter 1 section headings in orange and green (p.19); the hex is ours. The user's choice of 2026-10-12, over the brass the design review recommended. Text only: a notification's kicker and a readout's name line, never a fill and never body text. It shares a hue with health.good; the bar is a fill and the voice is text, and the user accepted the rhyme.

system.$description: The System's voice: a notification's kicker and a readout's name line

text.$description: Body text and values. Light is a brown-black ink on the parchment

text-muted.$description: Labels, formulas, secondary text. Still AA; never opacity

dcc.note: Oxblood, deeper than the D&D ampersand's red, in place of the classic orange (user, 2026-10-19, direction B). Dark is a brighter red because a deep red can't reach 4.5:1 as text on the dark grounds (5.42 / 5.00 / 4.52 here).

accent.$description: The one primary action on a screen, accent text, and the character's name on the band

focus.$description: The keyboard focus ring. Distinct from the accent so a focused primary button still shows its ring

dcc.note: Dark moved from #f06a5f to coral (2026-10-19), off the red accent it would otherwise match. Light is raspberry (user, 2026-10-23, the Journal pages concept's palette), in place of #b42318, which sat 2° of hue from the oxblood accent: 34° and ΔE00 18.7 off it now, and 6.28 / 7.04 / 5.47 as text on bg, surface and surface-raised.

danger.$description: Destructive actions and errors. Copy stays straight (spec §6.1)

health.$description: The Health Bar's three bands. The whole bar takes the colour of the band its level is in.

dcc.note: The book prints the band's colour name and range (green, 100% to 66%), not a hex value. The range is a rule and belongs in health-and-conditions.json; only the colour is here.
Yellow, 66% to 33%. Light theme uses a dark gold, because no true yellow reaches 3:1 on white.
Red, 33% to 0%.

empty.$description: A marked-off slot, and the empty track of the Mana Bar

dcc.note: The book names the Mana Bar (p.16) but prints no colour for it. Blue is our choice. Light darkened from #1f63c4 for the parchment's surface-raised (4.98).

Lapis, the user's pick of 2026-10-21 over mana blue, violet, verdigris and gold leaf: a deeper, inkier take on DCC's mana blue that sits with the oxblood and brown. Spell slots' own colour, so a slot never looks like a class resource's bronze use. Lowest pair 5.75 (light, on the spent track).

spell-slot.$description: A spell slot: filled while left, its outline once spent. In both looks

dcc.note: Gold leaf, the user's pick of 2026-10-21 for the Class resources section, beside lapis for spell slots. Dark is tier-gold's own; light is darker than tier-gold's #a8781a so a box holds 3:1 beside a spent one on parchment (3.46, the lowest pair).

class-resource.$description: A class resource's use (Rage, Second Wind, Arcane Recovery): filled while left, its outline once spent. In both looks

dcc.note: The novel's gold boxes glow with a golden light; the hex is ours. Of the three ceremony tiers only gold needs a colour: bronze is border-control, and Legendary is the accent at full screen (design review 2026-10-12).

tier-gold.$description: The gold tier's 2 px frame and glow: a level-up's notification

entity.$description: The minimap legend's colours for who is who. Unused in milestone 1; here because the book fixes their meaning and companions (orange) and any party or map view will need them.

dcc.note: Green Dot: Self.
Blue Dot: other crawlers, controlled by players or the GM.
Red Dot: hostile NPCs such as Mobs and Bosses.
White Dot: non-hostile NPCs. A white dot vanishes on a light canvas, so the light theme uses grey; the meaning is unchanged.
Purple Dot: non-crawlers and non-residents of the dungeon.
Orange Dot: pets and familiars. Close to the accent; they will need a shape as well as a colour when both appear together.

check.$description: The check type a skill is rolled as, from the book's check-type column (law 16): its row's left edge and symbol. The symbol carries the meaning (one die, two dice, a target, a hollow ring for Passive: no roll); colour is the second channel, and the type is also written on the row. Chosen by the user 2026-09-28: symbol and coloured edge.

dcc.note: Unopposed Check (p.59). Teal is our choice; the book prints no colour.
Opposed Check (p.59). Violet is our choice.
An Attack Skill, rolled against the target's Evade (p.110). Coral is our choice, kept off the danger red.
A Passive Skill: no Check, never rolled (p.173). Muted, since it asks nothing of the player.

journal.$description: The Adventurer's Journal look (Settings, Look; the journal concept, user 2026-10-20): a field book with a leather binding. Its grounds replace bg, surface, surface-raised, border, text-muted and health.empty while the look is on (index.css, [data-look='journal']); every other colour is the shared one, so its pairs are measured again on these grounds below. Light is the classic parchment's own values; dark is the concept's warm 'by candlelight' ground in place of the cool slate.

dcc.note: The concept's warm dark ground (2026-10-20). Light is the parchment bg.

surface.$description: A box or row on the page: the vitals, the tracker, a turn row

dcc.note: Dark lowered from the concept's chip #3d2c1f, which leaves the dark accent at 4.24 on it; #2b1f18 gives 4.59.

surface-raised.$description: A chip or a field inside a box

border.$description: Decorative hairline. Never the only thing that identifies a control

text-muted.$description: Labels and secondary text on the journal's grounds

track.$description: A spent slot or step, in place of health.empty

dcc.note: The binding: the band's top row and, on a wide screen, the cover around the open book. The concept's #4a2a18 in light; near black in dark, as its dark tile drew it.

The shelf (user, 2026-10-23, direction B of the Journal pages concept). The light binding's leather in both themes, as one hide would be: the dark binding's near-black vanishes on the dark page (1.06:1). The cover sits 1.43:1 off the dark page, so it is told by its frame and edge, not its fill.

cover.$description: The shelf's leather covers, and the cover round a page

dcc.note: The sheet (user, 2026-10-23, direction A of the sheet concept, its fixer's --a-plate). In dark, the raised paper a step toward the paper the shelf's plates are cut from (surface-raised 86%, on-leather 14%), so a plate lifts 1.65:1 off the dark page where the raised paper alone gave 1.15:1 and read as the boxed button it replaces. In light, the raised paper itself, which already stands off the page. Its words are the text and the muted text; the accent marks a plate only as a doubled rule, a graphic (3.19:1 in dark), never as words.

plate.$description: A label plate's paper on the sheet: Cast, a to-hit, a damage roll, Check, Save, a skill's total, the page's buttons

on-leather.$description: Words and marks on the leather: MENU, the folder, a name stamped on a cover

dcc.note: The light focus ring (#8f4a0e) is 1.93 on the light leather, so the binding and the covers use the dark theme's in both.

focus-on-leather.$description: The focus ring on the binding and the covers

stitch.$description: The binding's dashed stitching, decoration only there; on a cover, its tooled frame and a blank cover's photo mounts

dcc.note: A wax seal for the Rest buttons. Dark is a wax red of its own rather than the bright dark accent, which carries dark text: 3.08 on the dark page, 5.01 under its words. The first try, #8e1c16, was 2.03 on the page.

on-seal.$description: The words pressed into a seal

dcc.note: Drawn through a noise mask at low opacity: a warm glow on the dark page, brown flecks on the light one. Decoration only.

dice.$description: The dice the tray draws, and their numerals (the dice roll, approved by the user 2026-10-14; the five dice and four numeral colours chosen in Settings). A die is a thing, not a surface: each colour is one hex in both themes, so every numeral-on-die pair holds whatever the theme. Its edge is color.border-control, which gives it 3:1 against the tray in both themes (3.61 dark, 4.82 light); Mana blue's edge is the slate, as the mockup drew it, and its boundary holds by its fill on the dark tray (7.03) and by that edge on the light one (15.75). Each numeral pair below is measured on the die's own colour; the app offers a pair only where it also holds on the two facets of the d20 a numeral reaches, which its own test measures (src/dice/looks.test.ts). Not dice, each for a ruling: brass (the frame), green (the System's voice), the accent's red (the one primary action) and the check colours (law 16). The fourth numeral colour is gold leaf in place of DCC's orange #e8913a (user, 2026-10-23), and a device that saved Orange reads it as Gold leaf (src/settings.ts).

slate.$description: The default die (the user's choice, 2026-10-14): the HUD's own slate, the dark surface-raised as an object colour. Matte

bone.$description: Bone, and Marble's body under its veins. Polished

mana.$description: Mana blue. Polished, edged in the slate

coal.$description: Coal, darker than the slate. Matte

vein.$description: Marble's veins, drawn at 85 percent and kept clear of the numeral, so a numeral never sits on one

ink-light.$description: Light numerals, the default on Slate and Coal

ink-gold.$description: Gold leaf numerals, on Slate and Coal: the class resources' gold. 8.38 on Slate and 10.05 on Coal, 5.97 and 7.55 at the least on the d20's facets

ink-dark.$description: Ink numerals, the default on Bone and Mana blue

ink-engraved.$description: Engraved brass numerals, the default on Marble: dark enough to read on Bone (7.24), where the control brass gives 3.89

space.$description: A 4px step, in rem so it follows the user's font size.

display.$description: Headings in the Alegreya type style, the default (user, 2026-10-19, fonts 3): a sturdy small-caps serif, the body face's own family, set in mixed case so its small capitals show. The chrome's words take the body face. Never body text or long runs. An app self-hosts the font file and its SIL OFL licence; this token only names the family

display-beyond.$description: Headings and chrome in the Beyond type style, chosen in Settings (user, 2026-10-19, fonts 1): a tall condensed sans in capitals, as D&D Beyond's page titles

display-book.$description: Headings in the Book type style, chosen in Settings (user, 2026-10-19, fonts 2): a small-caps serif standing in for the books' Mrs Eaves, which is commercial. Set in mixed case, as display. Headings only; the chrome's words take the body face in this style

name.$description: The character's name on the band, in the accent, as a printed stat block's name: in the Alegreya style's face by default

name-book.$description: The character's name in the Beyond and Book styles, as the concept drew them

body.$description: Body text, values, and every number but a die's numeral, which follows the headings' face unless the player chooses otherwise in Settings (user, 2026-10-14). Alegreya Sans, a humanist sans with a calligraphic italic, standing in for the books' Scala Sans, which is commercial (user, 2026-10-19). Set with lining figures, since its default figures are old-style

hand.$description: The Adventurer's Journal's handwriting, for the words of the note tucked into the turn and nothing else (user, 2026-10-20). Never a number: a figure in the note keeps the body face. Caveat, SIL OFL, one self-hosted weight; it falls back to the body face, which the note's italic already suits

display.$description: The one Alegreya SC weight shipped; each extra weight is another file

display-beyond.$description: The one Roboto Condensed weight shipped

display-book.$description: The one Cormorant SC weight shipped; its lighter cuts thin out at heading sizes on a phone

hand.$description: Caveat's one shipped weight: 400 is too thin to read on parchment at a phone's size

font-size.$description: A small scale; the display face and body face are decided separately.

sm.$description: Labels and metadata. The floor: nothing smaller

default.$description: Every panel, slot, field, and button: crisp, after the inventory slots on p.19 (chosen 2026-09-27). Deliberately one value. Notched corners are kept for a single loud moment at most, because clip-path cuts off the focus ring

touch.$description: The minimum touch target, 44 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.5). The ten-slot Hotlist is the tightest case (spec §6.2)
